name: Associate Degree of Medical Laboratory Science
Bachelor of Agricultural Technology and Management
description:
UniSQ describes this as Queensland's first dedicated degree in agricultural technology and management, and the pitch is specific: it sits between traditional agricultural science and straight agribusiness, training students to apply precision-ag and digital technology to farm systems rather than just studying plant and animal science in the abstract or business theory divorced from paddock reality. Students based at Toowoomba get direct access to the working farming and agtech industries of the Darling Downs, one of Australia's most productive agricultural regions, and the course can also be completed externally for students already working in the sector.

At 24 units it's a leaner degree than most three-year bachelor's programs, built around agricultural science fundamentals (plant and animal production systems), the technology layer (precision agriculture, remote sensing, farm data systems), and the management side (agribusiness, supply chains, farm business decision-making). Work-integrated learning and industry placement units are built into the structure, which matters in a discipline where employers routinely rate practical exposure above classroom theory.

Graduates are aimed at roles in agronomy support, farm technology and precision-ag consulting, agribusiness management, and agricultural data analysis, a narrower but more targeted set of outcomes than a general agricultural science degree, reflecting the technology-and-management framing the course was actually built around.
curriculum:
Year 1: Plant production systems, animal production systems, introduction to agricultural technology, farm business fundamentals
Year 2: Precision agriculture and remote sensing, soil and water management, agribusiness and supply chains, agricultural data systems
Year 3: Farm business management and decision-making, industry placement/work-integrated learning, capstone agricultural technology project, elective units in a chosen specialisation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, no specific ATAR cut-off; suited to students from rural and regional backgrounds, with articulation pathways from the Diploma of Agriculture and Environmental Science Studies.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
UniSQ's Bachelor of Business follows the standard flexible-major structure most Australian business schools use now: a shared first-year core across accounting, economics, marketing, and management, then students pick a major: accounting, marketing, management, human resource management, tourism, or a handful of others, and build the back two years around it. What sets the delivery apart is less the content than the mode: a large share of the cohort studies wholly online, and the university has built its systems around that being the default rather than an add-on for people who can't make it to campus.

The degree carries professional accreditation pathways relevant to its majors, the accounting major is designed to meet the academic requirements for CPA Australia and CA ANZ membership, for instance, so students with a specific professional body in mind can check their major choice against that requirement early rather than discovering a gap in final year.

A capstone business project or internship unit toward the end of the degree gives students a chance to apply what they've studied to an actual organisational problem, and the university's regional business networks around Toowoomba and southeast Queensland feed a reasonable number of those placements.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting principles, economics, marketing fundamentals, management and organisational behaviour, business law, business statistics
Year 2: Major core units (accounting, marketing, management, HR, or tourism strand), business analytics, financial management
Year 3: Advanced major units, strategic management, capstone business project or industry placement, elective units
admission_requirements: Lowest adjusted ATAR to which UniSQ made an offer: 60.00 (no guarantee of admission at this score). Assumed knowledge: English (Units 3&4, C) and General Mathematics (Units 3&4, C).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, minimum 5.5 in each of listening, reading, writing and speaking (alternative English tests also accepted).

name: Bachelor of Design and Interactive Technologies
Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
Primary teaching at UniSQ is a four-year initial teacher education degree accredited against the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers, and it leads to registration as a primary school teacher on graduation. That's the standard shape for this qualification nationally, but UniSQ's version leans on its regional footprint for placement variety, with school partnerships across the Darling Downs, Ipswich, and wider southeast Queensland giving students a mix of regional and larger-town classroom experience rather than an exclusively metropolitan one.

Curriculum studies units cover the primary learning areas (literacy, numeracy, science, HASS, health and PE, the arts) alongside professional units in child development, inclusive education, and classroom management, with supervised professional experience placements building in length and responsibility each year, from observation-heavy early placements to a substantial final-year internship where students effectively run a classroom under a mentor teacher's supervision.

A sizeable share of the cohort studies externally, particularly students already working as teacher aides or in regional schools, and the degree is structured so placement blocks can be arranged around a student's existing location rather than requiring relocation to a university city.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child development, introduction to teaching and learning, foundations of literacy and numeracy, first professional experience placement
Year 2: Curriculum studies (English, mathematics, science), inclusive education, classroom management, professional experience placement
Year 3: Curriculum studies (HASS, the arts, health and PE), assessment and reporting, Indigenous perspectives in education, extended professional experience placement
Year 4: Advanced pedagogy, professional capstone unit, final internship placement (extended, near-autonomous teaching)
admission_requirements: Lowest adjusted ATAR to which UniSQ made an offer: 66.00. Assumed knowledge: English (Units 3&4, C) and General/Mathematical/Specialist Mathematics (Units 3&4, C). Satisfactory completion of LANTITE is required prior to final-year professional experience placement.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5, minimum 7.0 in writing and reading, minimum 8.0 in speaking and listening (alternative English tests also accepted).

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Ask most Queensland engineering academics who teaches the most students by distance and UniSQ's name comes up first: the university has run distance-education engineering programs for more than four decades and is Australia's largest provider of engineering degrees delivered off-campus. The Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is the degree that carries that reputation, and it shows in how the labs are built: UniSQ's Remote Access Laboratories let external students run real instrumentation and measurement experiments over the internet rather than substituting simulations for hands-on work.

Students choose a major from the usual spread (civil, electrical and electronic, mechanical, mechatronic, power, and others) and the degree is accredited by Engineers Australia, so graduates sit the same accreditation bar as anyone from a metro sandstone university. A supervised professional placement is built into the course, which matters more than it sounds for a program with a large external cohort: it's the mechanism that gets distance students onto an actual work site before graduation, not just into a classroom.

The university has also been ranked Australia's number one for graduate starting salary by the Good Universities Guide, a data point UniSQ leans on in its own marketing but which is at least consistent with an engineering-heavy graduate profile. Whether a given student is based in Toowoomba, Springfield, or studying entirely online from a mine site or a regional town, the course structure and assessment are designed to be identical, which is unusual enough among Australian engineering schools to be worth naming directly.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering mathematics and mechanics, engineering materials, engineering computing, professional engineering practice, discipline foundation units (statics, thermofluids, circuits depending on major)
Year 3: Major-specific core units (e.g. structural analysis for civil, power systems for electrical, machine design for mechanical), engineering management, project management
Year 4: Capstone engineering project (two-part), professional placement/work-integrated learning, advanced major electives, engineering law and ethics
Throughout: Remote Access Laboratory sessions and residential schools for practical/lab components
admission_requirements: Lowest adjusted ATAR to which UniSQ made an offer in Trimester 1, 2025: 69.50 (no guarantee of admission at this score). Assumed knowledge: English (Units 3&4, C) and Mathematical Methods (Units 3&4, C); Physics is recommended but not required; a Preparatory year is available for students who don't meet prerequisites.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, minimum 5.5 in each of listening, reading, writing and speaking (alternative English tests also accepted).

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
This is the entry-level computing degree UniSQ builds its whole postgraduate IT pipeline around. Finish it and the university explicitly points graduates toward its Master of Information Technology, Master of Data Science, or Master of Cyber Security as the next step, which tells you something about how the undergraduate course is structured: broad enough in first year to let students discover which specialisation actually interests them, then increasingly focused from second year on.

Majors run through the usual spread for a modern IT degree, including software development, cyber security, networking, data science and analytics, and programming-heavy units are backed by UniSQ's long-running remote/online lab infrastructure, the same systems that support its distance engineering cohort, so external students aren't working with a lesser version of the practical content.

A professional placement or capstone project unit near the end of the course gives students something concrete to point to in job interviews beyond a transcript, and the degree's accreditation alignment with the Australian Computer Society matters for students planning to chase ACS-recognised professional status after graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming fundamentals, computer systems, database fundamentals, web technologies, IT professional practice
Year 2: Major core units (software development, cyber security, networking, or data science strand), systems analysis and design, data structures and algorithms
Year 3: Advanced major electives, IT project management, capstone IT project or industry placement, emerging technologies elective
admission_requirements: Lowest adjusted ATAR to which UniSQ made an offer in Trimester 1, 2025: 58.90 (meeting this score does not guarantee admission).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, minimum 5.5 in each of listening, reading, writing and speaking (alternative English tests also accepted).

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing at UniSQ is delivered from a regional base (Toowoomba and Ipswich rather than inner-city Brisbane), which shapes where a lot of its clinical placements happen: students get real exposure to rural and regional health settings that metro-heavy nursing schools often can't offer as standard, alongside placements in larger hospital systems. The degree is accredited by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and graduates sit for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on completion.

The course structure follows the pattern most Australian nursing degrees use: foundational anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology units in first year, building toward specialty clinical units (mental health, paediatrics, aged care, acute care) in second and third year, with supervised clinical placement hours threaded through every year rather than saved for the end. UniSQ's placement network covers regional Queensland health services as well as metropolitan hospitals, which is a genuine point of difference for students who want experience in under-served health systems before they graduate into them.

Students who want to keep studying can move directly into UniSQ's Master of Nursing for a postgraduate specialisation, and the university markets a fairly direct undergraduate-to-postgraduate nursing pipeline for exactly that reason.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and physiology, foundations of nursing practice, pharmacology basics, communication in health care, introductory clinical placement
Year 2: Mental health nursing, medical-surgical nursing, pathophysiology, health assessment, clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Acute and critical care nursing, aged care and chronic illness, paediatric and family nursing, transition to professional practice, capstone clinical placement
Throughout: Supervised clinical placements across regional and metropolitan health settings, professional experience portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (Queensland Certificate of Education) or equivalent, no specific ATAR cut-off, plus a Health Undertaking and National Police Check; relevant recognition of prior learning available for enrolled nurses.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or equivalent (higher than most UniSQ programs due to nursing registration requirements).

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
UniSQ's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) is a four-year, APAC-accredited sequence built for students who already know they want provisional registration at the end of it, not just a psychology-adjacent arts degree. The first three years share a common set of foundational units with the university's other psych-flavoured degrees, so students who start here and change their mind about the honours pathway aren't locked in early. The divergence happens later, once the fourth-year research component kicks in.

That fourth year is where the degree earns its name. Students complete an honours research project (PSY4000) alongside units in advanced research methods, ethical and professional practice, and applied assessment and intervention skills, working under the supervision of academic staff who are themselves practising or research psychologists. Because a large share of UniSQ's cohort studies externally, the clinical and assessment skills components are built around structured on-campus intensives and simulated client work rather than assuming everyone is walking past a psych clinic on campus daily.

Graduates come out eligible for provisional registration as a psychologist with AHPRA, which is the real value proposition of choosing the Honours pathway over a plain Bachelor's: it's the entry ticket to supervised practice or further postgraduate study toward general or clinical registration. UniSQ explicitly positions this degree as a pipeline into its own Master of Professional Psychology, so students planning that far ahead can map out a five-plus-one style progression from day one.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Lifespan Development, Social Psychology, foundational research methods and statistics units
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Psychological Measurement, Abnormal Psychology, Personality Theory, intermediate quantitative and qualitative research methods
Year 3: Health Psychology, Psychology of Learning, Applied research design, discipline elective units, work-integrated learning options
Year 4 (Honours): PSY4111 Advanced Research Approaches, PSY4020 Ethical and Professional Practice, PSY4040 Psychological Interventions, PSY4070 Assessment and Interview Skills, PSY4000 Psychology Honours Project (thesis)
admission_requirements: Minimum ATAR of 68.25 (or equivalent qualification) per UniSQ's handbook; entry into the honours component is additionally competitive, based on GPA in earlier years.

name: Graduate Certificate of Sport and Exercise
Master of Business Administration
description:
UniSQ's MBA follows the generalist model most Australian MBAs use: core units across strategy, finance, marketing, leadership, and organisational behaviour, aimed at experienced professionals moving into or already working in management roles rather than fresh graduates. Where it departs from the metro-university MBA template is delivery: it's built primarily for students studying externally while working full-time, which shapes the assessment design around applied, workplace-relevant projects rather than assuming students have time for extended residential intensives.

Students typically bring several years of workplace experience into the cohort, and case studies and group assignments lean on that mix of industries and seniority levels rather than assuming a uniform corporate background. A capstone strategic management project toward the end of the degree asks students to apply the accumulated coursework to a real organisational problem, often drawn from their own workplace.

The degree doesn't chase the specific big-name accreditations (AACSB, EQUIS) that the most prestige-focused Australian MBAs market heavily, and is positioned instead as an accessible, flexible option for regional and remote professionals who need postgraduate business credentials without relocating or taking time off work.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic management, managerial finance, marketing management, organisational behaviour and leadership, business economics, operations management
Elective units: Selected from specialisations such as project management, human resource management, or international business
Capstone: Strategic management project (applied, often workplace-based)
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree plus at least two years of professional work experience, or a graduate certificate/diploma in a related discipline; delivered fully online.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.
intake_dates: February, April, July, September, November (online, multiple study periods)

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science runs on twelve core ICT and analytics units rather than a long menu of loosely related electives, which keeps the degree tight: statistics, machine learning, big data systems, and data visualisation are treated as the spine of the course rather than optional add-ons bolted onto a generic IT masters. Students coming in with an undergraduate background outside computing typically pick up a set of foundation units first to bring their programming and stats up to postgraduate speed before moving into the specialist content.

What distinguishes it from a lot of similarly-named degrees elsewhere is that it's taught by a university that has spent decades building distance-delivery infrastructure, so the heavily technical, lab-based components (model building, data pipeline work, visualisation projects) are designed from the ground up for students working through them off-campus, often while employed full-time. A capstone project lets students apply the full analytics pipeline to a real or realistic dataset, which is the piece employers tend to ask about at interview.

Graduates leave positioned for data analyst, data engineer, or junior data scientist roles, and the degree sits alongside UniSQ's Master of Information Technology and Master of Cyber Security as one of three postgraduate computing options the university actively cross-promotes to its own IT undergraduates.
curriculum:
Foundation units (where required): Programming fundamentals, database systems, introductory statistics
Core: Data wrangling and management, statistical modelling, machine learning, big data technologies, data visualisation, data ethics and governance, cloud computing for data science
Capstone: Data science project (industry or research-based)
Maximum candidature: six years part-time, allowing for concurrent full-time work
admission_requirements: Completion of an Australian university 3-year bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in any discipline, OR a minimum of 5 years' professional work experience equivalent to an AQF Level 7 (bachelor) qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, minimum 5.5 in each of listening, reading, writing and speaking (alternative English tests also accepted).

name: Master of Education
description:
UniSQ's Master of Education is aimed at people already teaching, not career-changers looking for an initial qualification. It's a postgraduate degree for practising educators who want to specialise or move into leadership, and the course design assumes students are working full-time in schools while they study. Specialisation strands typically cover areas like educational leadership, TESOL, inclusive education, and curriculum studies, and students can usually shape a chunk of the degree around whichever of those matches their actual career direction.

Because the degree sits within a university whose delivery model has been built around distance and online study for decades, assessment is structured around what a working teacher can realistically produce alongside a full timetable: applied projects and research tied to the student's own school context rather than requiring long stretches of campus attendance.

A research-focused exit option (often a minor thesis or major project) exists for teachers considering a later move into doctoral study or educational research roles, alongside the more common coursework-only completion for those staying in the classroom or moving into middle leadership.
curriculum:
Core units: Educational research methods, contemporary issues in education, leading learning and teaching
Specialisation units (select strand): Educational leadership, TESOL, inclusive and special education, or curriculum and pedagogy
Elective units: Drawn from education specialisations or cross-disciplinary options
Exit options: Coursework-only completion, or research project/minor thesis pathway for those considering further postgraduate research
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, normally in education or a related field, or a bachelor degree plus relevant professional teaching experience; designed for practising teachers seeking specialisation or career progression.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0, or equivalent (reflecting teacher registration requirements).

name: Master of Nursing
description:
This is UniSQ's postgraduate specialisation route for registered nurses who've finished their undergraduate degree and want to move into advanced clinical practice, education, or leadership rather than staying at generalist RN level indefinitely. It's built for working nurses: the majority of the cohort studies externally while holding down clinical shifts. Specialisation strands typically include areas like nurse practitioner preparation, clinical leadership, or nurse education, depending on which stream a student enrols in.

Coursework covers advanced clinical assessment, evidence-based practice, and health systems leadership, with a research or applied project component that lets students investigate a genuine clinical or workplace issue rather than a hypothetical one. Given UniSQ's Bachelor of Nursing graduates are steered toward this degree as the next step, there's a reasonably well-worn pathway from RN registration through to postgraduate specialisation within the one institution.

Students pursuing the nurse practitioner stream complete additional advanced practice and prescribing units alongside supervised clinical hours, positioning them for endorsement as nurse practitioners, a role with growing demand in the regional and rural health services UniSQ's own placement network already covers.
curriculum:
Core units: Advanced health assessment, evidence-based practice, health systems and leadership, research methods for nursing
Specialisation strand: Nurse practitioner preparation (advanced pharmacology, diagnostics, prescribing) or clinical leadership/education strand
Applied/research component: Clinical project or minor research thesis
For NP stream: Supervised advanced clinical practice placements
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a health-related discipline (a non-nursing entry pathway is available), or a Bachelor of Nursing for registered nurses seeking advanced standing; current registration or eligibility for registration with AHPRA required for the nursing-entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or equivalent, consistent with nursing registration standards.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description:
This is the degree UniSQ points its own Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) graduates toward, and it functions as the next rung on the registration ladder for students who've done the four-year undergraduate sequence and want to keep moving toward broader practice rights rather than stopping at provisional registration. The course combines advanced coursework in assessment, intervention, and professional ethics with a substantial supervised practicum placement: the applied hours are the actual point of the degree, not a formality attached to it.

Students work with clients under supervision as part of the practicum component, building the direct-practice hours AHPRA expects to see before general registration, and the coursework side covers assessment techniques, evidence-based interventions, and the professional and ethical frameworks that govern psychological practice in Australia.

Because UniSQ runs a large distance cohort, the placement component is coordinated across a wider geographic spread of supervising psychologists and services than a metro-only program would need, which in practice means students in regional Queensland aren't stuck waiting for a city-based placement to open up.
curriculum:
Core coursework: Advanced psychological assessment, evidence-based interventions, professional ethics and practice standards, psychopathology
Applied component: Supervised practicum placement (staged across the degree, building client contact hours)
Research component: Applied research project or case-based research unit
Professional development: Practice management and supervision seminars
admission_requirements: An Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) accredited four-year psychology qualification (e.g. Bachelor of Psychology Honours) with a credit average or better; competitive entry due to limited places.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0, or equivalent.
